title: The Slow Tide
premise: For ten years, Ada Oyelaran has received anonymous letters correcting the endings of her unpublished manuscripts — letters that understood her grief better than anyone alive. When the writer, Elias Marsh, finally moves into the crumbling cottage next door, he brings a secret: he was the court clerk who buried the evidence that cleared her grandfather of the lighthouse negligence charge that ruined the family, and the letters were his penance. As Ada and Elias fall in love over one fading coastal summer, she must decide whether the justice she's owed is worth the man she's found, and whether belonging means keeping the lighthouse her grandmother left her or burning it down. In the end, Ada publishes the truth in her first novel and chooses Elias — not because he deserves forgiveness, but because she deserves a future bigger than her grievance.
about_author: Kestrel Reyes is a former maritime archivist who spent six years cataloguing lighthouse logs along the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted fog-signal station in Maine, where she still answers reader letters by hand.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On the anniversary of her grandfather's death, Ada receives the tenth anonymous letter correcting her manuscript's ending, just as the last train of the season pulls out of the coastal station. Emotional beat: lonely ritual disrupted by the sense that the letters' author is closer than ever.

chapters.title: The Cottage Next Door
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A moving van arrives at the long-abandoned Marsh cottage; Ada watches from her grandmother's lighthouse gallery and recognizes the new tenant's handwriting on a box labeled FRAGILE — the same slanted capitals as the letters. Beat: suspicion kindling alongside curiosity.

chapters.title: Salt and Ink
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias unpacks a decade of unsent drafts and the sealed court file he stole on his last day as a clerk, telling himself he came to confess, not to be known. Beat: guilt dressed up as courage, already failing.

chapters.title: Borrowed Light
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A storm knocks out the cottage power; Elias appears at the lighthouse door asking to borrow a lamp, and they talk until dawn about novels, tides, and second chances — carefully, on his side, avoiding the past. Beat: first warmth, first lie of omission.

chapters.title: What the Letters Knew
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Rereading all ten letters, Ada realizes only someone who knew her grandfather could have written them; she tests Elias at the market with a detail from the letters and watches him flinch. Beat: the hunt begins, tangled with attraction.

chapters.title: The Negligence File
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Flashback to 2014: young clerk Elias discovers the exculpatory maintenance log, is ordered by his superior to bury it, and obeys — then begins writing to Ada under a pen name as penance. Beat: the wound that explains the man.

chapters.title: Low Tide, Long Walk
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Elias helps Ada repair the lighthouse's storm-damaged seawall; working side by side, they trade stories about family, and Ada almost tells him about the letters but holds back. Beat: intimacy deepening on a foundation of mutual concealment.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Will
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A lawyer arrives with Ada's late grandmother's will: the lighthouse is hers only if she lives in it year-round for two years — otherwise it goes to a developer. Beat: belonging becomes a deadline, echoing the blurb's running clock.

chapters.title: The Manuscript in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias finds Ada's abandoned manuscript in the shared boathouse and recognizes his own marginal notes quoted back in her revisions; he realizes she's been writing to him too, without knowing it. Beat: awe curdling into terror of exposure.

chapters.title: Harvest Supper
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The town's harvest dinner; Ada's old rival, journalist Priya Nair, announces she's investigating the Oyelaran case for a cold-justice podcast. Elias goes pale; Ada defends him without knowing why. Beat: outside pressure arrives, triangle of secrets tightens.

chapters.title: Almost Telling
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. On the lighthouse gallery at night, Elias nearly confesses; Ada, misreading his silence as hesitation about their romance, kisses him instead. Beat: the confession swallowed by the kiss — tenderness and dread in one breath.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The developer offers Ada enough money to escape her debts if she signs before the season's end, the same week her residency deadline looms; Elias urges her to refuse, and she snaps that he has no right to know what she owes. Beat: money, pride, and love collide.

chapters.title: Priya's Questions
chapters.summary: Priya's POV (single interlude). Priya interviews townsfolk about the 2014 lighthouse death and learns a court clerk requested the file years ago — and then vanished from the records. Beat: the noose of the subplot tightens around Elias from outside the romance.

chapters.title: What He Kept
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada finds the stolen court file in Elias's cottage while returning a borrowed book — her grandfather's name, the buried maintenance log, Elias's clerk signature. Beat: the floor drops out; love and betrayal become the same document.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Light
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada summons Elias to the lantern room and demands everything; he confesses fully — the buried evidence, the letters, the move — and offers her the file, his testimony, and his departure. Beat: climax of truth; Ada sends him away without an answer.

chapters.title: The Empty Cottage
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Elias packs to leave; Ada watches the cottage windows go dark and rereads the first letter, seeing not penance but a decade of someone trying to become worthy. Beat: grief without anger, the turn toward choice.

chapters.title: Justice, Unofficial
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada gives Priya the file — on the condition the story centers the town's complicity, not just Elias's; the podcast greenlights the exoneration push. Beat: Ada claims justice on her own terms, outside the courts that failed her.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias testifies to the state review board, surrendering his career and name to the record; afterward he waits at the empty station platform, certain he's lost her. Beat: sacrifice completed, hope nearly extinguished.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The developer's signing deadline and her residency deadline land the same day; Ada refuses the buyout, chooses the lighthouse, and finishes her novel with a new ending — one where the letter-writer stays. Beat: both inheritances claimed at once.

chapters.title: Exoneration
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The board posthumously clears her grandfather; the town gathers at the lighthouse as the flag is raised and her grandmother's name is read aloud beside his. Beat: public restoration, private still unfinished.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Letter
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. At the station, Elias writes an eleventh letter he doesn't intend to send; Ada arrives before the last train — the season's final one — and answers it aloud: stay. Beat: the blurb's promise kept; forgiveness as decision, not feeling.

chapters.title: Year-Round
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue tone. One year later: her novel is published with both their names in the acknowledgments, Elias has repaired the cottage, and the two houses share one light. Beat: belonging chosen, not inherited — the slow tide finally come in.
